profile.headline: Ph.D. in Bioinformatics @Institute for Data Science & Informatics, University of Missouri - Columbia
profile.summary:
I'm an enthusiastic bioinformatician eager to contribute to team success through hard work, attention to detail, and excellent organizational skills. Effective at compiling and interpreting bioinformatics information by leveraging software, statistics, and data mining. I am motivated to learn and excel in current trends, technological advances, and new techniques in bioinformatics.

I received a BS degree in Crop Science from the Vietnam National University of Agriculture and a diploma in Software Engineering from Hanoi Aptech Computer Education. After college, I worked as a software engineer for three years. Then I sought graduate programs in Bioinformatics, which aligned with my interest in genetics and computer. I ended up joining the lab of Dr. Christine Elsik at the University of Missouri, Columbia. Here, I learned so much about genome sequence analysis and the development of genome databases. My research centered around using bioinformatics approaches to understand the genome evolution of honey bees. I received my Ph.D. in May 2022.

positions.title: Doctoral Student
positions.description:
Graduate Student with Dr. Christine Elsik Lab
My Ph.D. Research: Investigating genome composition of eusocial Hymenopteran insects.
I also participated in multiple projects within the lab and with collaborators including: 
     - Developing genome databases for Bovine, Hymenoptera, and Maize.
     - Assembling new genome for the dwarf honey bee (Apis florea) and the giant honey bee (Apis dorsata) 
     - Identifying candidate genes for a temperature-sensitive miniature phenotype in Soybean

Teaching experience - I was the teaching assistant for the following courses during my Ph.D. time at the University of Missouri:
     - Biology of Animal Production 
     - Introduction to bioinformatics programming

projects.title: Investigating Genome Compositional Features of Apis and other Hymenopteran Insects
projects.description:
In this project, we resolved the evolutionary history of GC compositional features in Apis and other Hymenopteran Insects genome: 
·	Use the IsoPlotter algorithm to segment genomes into GC compositional domains for twenty-seven insect species with different levels of social complexity.
·	Use Perl and R for statistical analysis of GC distribution of compositional domains in Apis and other Hymenopteran Insects genome
·	Use GeneMerge and GOView tool for Gene Ontology enrichment analysis of genes in different GC compositional domains
·	Use OrthoDB pipeline, MCScanX algorithm, and Perl to identify and analyze synteny and gene duplication in correlation with GC compositional domains

projects.title: Missouri Epscor - The Missouri Transect: Climate, Plants and Community
projects.description:
Project: The Missouri Transect: Climate, Plants and Community addresses a fundamental issue in sustainability and resilience - how plants and crops adapt to increased climate variability. The project seeks to associate plant genotypes and phenotypes with environmental variability, with the end goal of improved crop production.
I was a member of the Cyberinfrastructure Team who collaborated with the research and education teams and leveraged existing resources to increase high-performance computing, storage, and visualization capabilities through EPSCoR servers. My role in the Cyberinfrastructure Team:
·	Maintain the EPSCoR servers
·	Manage researcher data
·	Develop and maintain the EPSCoR websites
